title: Five-year Local Option Levy for Police, Fire & 911 Operations.
ballot_label: Caption: Five-year Local Option Levy for Police, Fire & 911 Operations. Question: Shall Troutdale adopt a local option levy at $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value for police, fire & 911 services? This measure may cause property taxes to increase more than three percent.
summary: Troutdale contracts for police, fire and 911 services. This five-year local option levy of $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value would fund only police, fire and 911 operations, and the Council would replace the current $25 Public Safety Fee. The City says costs are rising faster than available funding and projects a $3 million gap next year growing to over $5 million by 2030.
yes_means: A yes vote approves a five-year Troutdale local option property tax levy of $1.60 per $1,000 of assessed value for police, fire and 911 services.
no_means: A no vote rejects the proposed five-year levy for police, fire and 911 services.
fiscal_impact: Per the ballot summary: estimated collections $3,556,392 (2027-28), $3,663,084 (2028-29), $3,772,977 (2029-30), $3,886,166 (2030-31) and $4,002,751 (2031-32). An average Troutdale home assessed at about $267,800 would pay about $428.48 a year; because the current Public Safety Utility Fee (about $300 a year) would be eliminated, the summary estimates a net annual increase of about $128.48.

arguments.author: City of Troutdale (explanatory statement, submitted by Sarah Skroch, City Recorder)
arguments.statement: The City's explanatory statement says current trends show a $3 million public safety funding gap next year, growing to over $5 million by 2030.
arguments.excerpt: Current trends show a $3 million funding gap next year increasing annually to over $5 million by 2030.

arguments.author: Mayor David Ripma
arguments.statement: In a 2026 KATU interview, Mayor David Ripma said that if voters reject the levy the city would be in fiscal trouble and would have to figure something out.
arguments.excerpt: Ripma told KATU that if voters reject the property tax levy, the city would be in "fiscal trouble." "We'll have to figure something out," he said.

arguments.author: Eric Anderson, former Troutdale City Councilor
arguments.statement: Former Troutdale City Councilor Eric Anderson argues the five-year levy is a temporary measure and that the City should finish its service-agreement restructuring before asking taxpayers for more.
arguments.excerpt: A temporary tax does not fix the underlying cost structure; it buys five years while taxpayers pay more.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Nov 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet, p. M-93)

gaps: No argument in favor was filed in the county voters' pamphlet (M-92: 'No arguments in favor of this measure were filed'); the only YES-side items are the City's explanatory statement and a mayor interview.
collection_notes: Updated 2026-10-16 from the Multnomah County voters' pamphlet extract (M-92 ballot title and explanatory statement, M-93 arguments). One argument in opposition was filed (Eric Anderson) and none in favor. The official summary describes the fee as '$25 Public Safety Fee' / '$25 per month Public Safety Utility Fee' and the average annual fee as $300; fiscal_impact now cites the pamphlet rather than KATU. The Sept 8, 2026 argument deadline has passed per the county filings page. Measure document PDFs on multco.us (measure_26-26x/download, referral documents) have no machine-readable text (scanned). WebFetch limits quotes to 125 characters, so several excerpts are sentence segments. yes_means/no_means are not official text: Oregon local ballot titles have no official result-of-vote statement, so they are neutral one-sentence descriptions written strictly from the official ballot question. Inventory title, number and jurisdiction (City of Troutdale) match the multco.us page and filings list (filed 8/12/2026). The ballot summary calls the fee the '$25 Public Safety Fee' while the explanatory statement calls it the 'Public Safety Utility Fee'; KATU describes it as $300 a year (likely $25/month; not stated by the City). troutdaleoregon.gov notice pages redirect to a login page. y1 is from the City-authored explanatory statement (kind explainer), not a filed argument. KGW and KOIN articles on the related police-department question returned fetch errors. The same search set was run for yes and no.
